title: RideLink Meal Days on the First and Last Days of Travel — Counting Standard
content:
On a Non-Emergency Medical Transportation long-distance stay, the first and last days of travel are partly spent on the road, and they count toward meals according to how long the drive is.

**Rule.** The first and last travel days of a stay count toward meals at a share set by the longest registered one-way miles among the trip's legs: under the mid-drive miles of 150, each of the two counts at the short-drive share of 0.5 of a day; from 150 miles up to but not including the full-day-drive miles of 300, each counts at the mid-drive share of 0.75 of a day; at or above 300 miles, each counts in full. Every travel day between them counts in full, so the meal days are the travel days less twice the part of an edge day that is not counted.

The one-way miles are those registered on the legs that carry the trip's reservation number; the longest of them decides the share.

## Distance bands

| Longest registered one-way miles | Each of the first and last travel days counts as | Meal days, for a stay of N travel days |
|---|---|---|
| Under 150 | 0.5 of a day | N less 1 |
| 150 to 299 | 0.75 of a day | N less 0.5 |
| 300 or more | A full day | N |

## Boundary pairs

*Hypothetical distances:* 149 miles falls under 150 and gives 0.5; 150 miles gives 0.75. 299 miles still gives 0.75; 300 miles gives a full day.

## Worked figures

*Hypothetical stay of 4 travel days:*

- longest leg 130 miles: 4 travel days less twice 0.5 gives 3 meal days;
- longest leg 200 miles: 4 travel days less twice 0.25 gives 3.5 meal days;
- longest leg 320 miles: all 4 travel days are meal days.
